source_refs.note: Topic 27.3.1 (PDF 168); an original sketch of the three effects is added. The book's single pH range is reported with a note on pepsin.

blocks.text: The activity of an enzyme is affected mainly by temperature, pH and the concentrations of substrate and enzyme; it can also be affected by other substances such as co-enzymes, activators and inhibitors.

items: Temperature and pH: the temperature and pH that give maximum activity are the optimum temperature and optimum pH. Moving away from these values can deactivate the enzyme. Enzymes in the human body work best at about 37 C and a pH range of 6.4-6.9.

Concentration of enzyme and substrate: the rate increases as the enzyme or substrate concentration increases, because more binding sites are used and more enzyme-substrate complex forms. However, increasing the substrate concentration beyond a limit can slow down the reaction.
